official.description_text:
PhD students in Computer Vision to estimate breathing and pulse from video
Apply for position
KTH Royal Institute of Technology, School of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science
Project description
Third-cycle subject:
Computer Science
The goal of this project is to develop video-based methods to monitor a human’s physiological parameters such as heart rate, breathing pattern, skin temperature, pupil dilation, etc. Physiological responses can be used to infer underlying states such as concentration, anxiety, and depression, and are more difficult to control for the human than explicit behaviors (e.g. facial expressions and speech). Working systems in clinical and cognitive-scientific practice typically require intrusive devices, so our video-based solution would be both scientifically novel and practically useful. The project will be performed in collaboration with perceptual neuroscience researchers at Karolinska Institutet in Solna, Sweden
Supervision:
Hedvig Kjellström is proposed to supervise the doctoral student. Decisions are made on admission.
Admission requirements
To be admitted to postgraduate education (Chapter 7, 39 § Swedish Higher Education Ordinance), the applicant must have basic eligibility in accordance with either of the following:
passed a second cycle degree (for example a master's degree), or
completed course requirements of at least 240 higher education credits, of which at least 60 second-cycle higher education credits, or
acquired, in some other way within or outside the country, substantially equivalent knowledge
The applicant to this position must also have a Master degree with a major in Machine Learning, Artificial Intelligence, Signal Processing or Computer Vision.
In addition to the above, there is also a
mandatory requirement for English equivalent to English B/6.
Selection
In order to succeed as a doctoral student at KTH you need to be goal oriented and persevering in your work. During the selection process, candidates will be assessed upon their ability to:
independently pursue his or her work
collaborate with others,
have a professional approach and
analyze and work with complex issues,
For this position, we put great emphasis on the ability to present documented experience in machine learning, especially programming of deep neural networks. The candidate should also have documented experience in computer vision, image processing, or signal processing.
Moreover, experience with medical applications and experience with 3D analysis of humans in video are meriting.
After the qualification requirements, great emphasis will be placed on personal skills.
Target degree:
Doctoral degree
Information regarding admission and employment
Only those admitted to postgraduate education may be employed as a doctoral student. The total length of employment may not be longer than what corresponds to full-time doctoral education in four years' time. An employed doctoral student can, to a limited extent (maximum 20%), perform certain tasks within their role, e.g. training and administration. A new position as a doctoral student is for a maximum of one year, and then the employment may be renewed for a maximum of two years at a time. In the case of studies that are to be completed with a licentiate degree, the total period of employment may not be longer than what corresponds to full-time doctoral education for two years.

ai.summary: Doctoral position in computer vision and machine learning focused on video-based physiological parameter estimation (heart rate, breathing, skin temperature, pupil dilation) to infer cognitive and emotional states, in collaboration with perceptual neuroscience researchers at Karolinska Institutet.

thematic_fit.rationale: Limited thematic overlap. The position concerns computer vision and physiological signal processing for cognitive/emotional state inference. The researcher's interests are spatial cognition, wayfinding, and collaborative immersive interaction—not physiological sensing or cognitive state inference. While both touch HCI broadly, the research question and application domain are fundamentally different.

methodological_fit.rationale: Partial but weak methodological fit. The position requires deep expertise in machine learning, deep neural networks, image processing, and signal processing—domains where the researcher has beginner-level Python skills and no documented experience in computer vision or ML algorithm development. The researcher's strength is in XR application development and user study design, not in algorithmic development or signal processing. The collaboration with perceptual neuroscience adds a human-science component, but does not bridge the core technical gap.

growth_value.rationale: Moderate-low growth value. Completing this PhD would develop strong machine learning and computer vision skills, which could theoretically enhance future human-computer interaction research. However, it would not advance spatial cognition, wayfinding, or collaborative immersive systems expertise. The researcher would gain physiological sensing capability (listed as missing), but at the cost of three years without developing XR design, multiplayer systems, or spatial-learning methodologies. The deviation is too large to justify as strategic skill-building for the target identity.

strategic_value.rationale: Moderate strategic value with significant constraints. KTH is well-regarded, and collaboration with Karolinska Institutet adds multidisciplinary credibility. However: (1) the supervisor (Hedvig Kjellström) is a computer vision specialist, not an HCI researcher, limiting mentorship for human-centred work; (2) the position does not advance toward Aalto or TU Delft, the researcher's priority targets; (3) the location (Stockholm) is geographically acceptable but not within preferred countries (Finland, Netherlands). The degree is valuable but does not open doors to target institutions or groups.

required_skills: machine-learning (not in taxonomy, inferred from 'deep neural networks')
computer-vision (not in taxonomy, listed as required)
eligibility_flags: Posting mandates 'Master degree with a major in Machine Learning, Artificial Intelligence, Signal Processing or Computer Vision.' Researcher's MSc is in Multimedia and Creative Multimedia with focus on human-centred XR, not AI/ML/vision. Eligibility hinges on whether the specific research focus (multiplayer XR systems) qualifies as 'substantially equivalent knowledge' under Swedish ordinance—likely negative.

Posting emphasizes 'documented experience in machine learning, especially programming of deep neural networks' and 'documented experience in computer vision, image processing, or signal processing.' Researcher has none of these.
Researcher's MSc is still in progress (thesis stage). Admission depends on thesis completion and degree conferral before admission deadline (27.Sep.2026).
risks: Mandatory degree requirement (ML/AI/Vision major) is unlikely to be met by a Multimedia Engineering degree; application may be desk-rejected.
Computer vision and deep learning are explicitly listed in the researcher's excluded directions ('pure-computer-vision'). This position violates the declared constraint.
Steep learning curve: researcher would need to rapidly develop expertise in deep neural networks, image processing, and signal processing—areas with no prior experience.
Supervisor (computer vision specialist) does not align with human-centred HCI mentorship needs.
Three years in computer vision would further delay return to spatial cognition and immersive learning research, extending time to target identity.
No clear pathway to future HCI/XR positions after this degree; may be pigeonholed as a vision researcher.
